articles.title: Notebook na Black Friday: Como escolher processador, RAM e SSD | G1
articles.standfirst: Veja quais especificações realmente importam na hora da compra e entenda como processador, memória RAM, SSD, placa de vídeo e tela influenciam no desempenho e no preço do notebook.
articles.summary: Avalie processador, memória RAM e SSD para comprar o notebook ideal na Black Friday e garanta o melhor desempenho para trabalho, estudos ou jogos sem gastar demais.
articles.body:
Na hora de comprar um notebook em época de Black Friday, entender termos como SSD, memória RAM e geração do processador faz diferença.

São esses componentes que ajudam a definir se a máquina será suficiente para estudar, trabalhar, navegar na internet ou rodar jogos e até mesmo recursos de inteligência artificial.

A escolha correta pode garantir melhor desempenho e evitar gastos desnecessários com um modelo acima — ou abaixo — do que você realmente precisa. Veja abaixo o que significa cada termo.

O processador é o “cérebro” do notebook. Quanto mais poderoso e eficiente ele for, mais rápido e fluido tende a ser o desempenho em tarefas como abrir programas, navegar na web, editar arquivos ou jogar.

Um notebook para estudar, por exemplo, não precisa do mesmo nível de potência de um modelo voltado para games, que exige mais desempenho para rodar sem travamentos.

As marcas mais comuns em notebooks com Windows são Intel, AMD e Qualcomm. Já a Apple usa chips próprios nos computadores com macOS.

No caso da Intel, vale prestar atenção à geração e à linha do chip. Entre os modelos mais atuais estão os Intel Core Ultra (3, 5, 7 e 9), já prontos para uso com IA por terem um processador dedicado para isso, chamado NPU.

Também ainda aparecem no mercado notebooks com chips Core (i3, i5, i7 e i9) de 11ª, 12ª, 13ª e 14ª gerações.

Na AMD, os chips mais recentes da linha para notebooks são os Ryzen AI e as linhas 3, 5, 7 e 9.

De forma geral, tanto na Intel quanto na AMD, quanto maior o número da família, maior tende a ser o desempenho. Um processador da linha 7, por exemplo, costuma ser mais potente que um da linha 3.

Isso também influencia no preço: um notebook com Core i3 ou Ryzen 3 normalmente será mais barato do que um com Core 7 Ultra ou Ryzen AI 400.

Nos modelos da Apple, os chips mais conhecidos vão do M1 ao M6, o mais recente.

Notebooks com Qualcomm Snapdragon usam uma arquitetura diferente, e alguns programas e jogos podem não funcionar.

A memória RAM é o espaço usado pelo sistema e pelos aplicativos para acessar informações rapidamente durante o uso.

A regra, aqui, é simples: quanto mais RAM, melhor.

Modelos mais baratos costumam vir com 4 GB, mas o mínimo recomendável hoje é 8 GB. Se você quer rodar qualquer sistema de inteligência artificial, vá de 16 GB pelo menos.

Bom lembrar que, para usar os recursos de inteligência artificial integrados ao Windows, nos chamados Copilot+ PCs, a Microsoft exige pelo menos 16 GB.

O ideal é escolher um notebook com SSD, sigla para unidade de estado sólido. Esse tipo de armazenamento é mais rápido do que o HD convencional , o que ajuda o computador a ligar mais depressa e a abrir programas com mais agilidade.

O mínimo de capacidade costuma ser 256 GB , já que o sistema e as atualizações ocupam uma parte considerável desse espaço.

Por isso, vale a mesma lógica de que quanto maior a capacidade, melhor, principalmente para guardar fotos, vídeos, documentos e aplicativos.

A placa de vídeo, também chamada de GPU, é responsável pelo processamento gráfico do computador — como imagens, vídeos, efeitos visuais e jogos.

Integrada: compartilha recursos com o restante do sistema

Dedicada: tem processamento próprio e costuma oferecer mais desempenho

Em geral, quanto mais avançada a placa de vídeo, mais caro será o notebook.

O tamanho da tela deve ser escolhido de acordo com o tipo de uso.

Um notebook de 15 polegadas costuma ser uma opção equilibrada para estudar e trabalhar, porque ainda cabe na mochila e pode ser transportado com relativa facilidade.

Já modelos com 17 polegadas são menos práticos para levar no dia a dia, mas oferecem mais espaço para ver vídeos, trabalhar com janelas maiores e jogar em tela cheia.

Também é importante observar a resolução. O recomendável é que a tela seja Full HD (1.920 x 1.080 pixels), o que garante mais nitidez e detalhes. Modelos mais baratos costumam vir com resolução HD.

Nos notebooks gamers, outro ponto importante é a taxa de atualização da tela, como 120 Hz ou 144 Hz. Esse número indica quantas vezes a imagem é atualizada por segundo. Quanto maior a taxa, mais fluida tende a ser a experiência, especialmente em jogos.

Confira as especificações antes de comprar

As fabricantes costumam vender notebooks com o mesmo nome, mas com configurações diferentes. Isso pode causar variações significativas de preço entre lojas.

Alguns fabricantes oferecem versões mais baratas de notebooks com sistema operacional Linux, principalmente nas configurações de entrada.

Isso pode não ser um problema para quem usa o computador apenas para navegar na internet e editar textos. Mas pode ser um obstáculo para quem precisa de programas específicos para Windows ou quer jogar.

Na hora da compra, vale verificar se o notebook já vem com o Windows 11, a versão mais recente do sistema da Microsoft, instalada de fábrica.

articles.title: Soldado dá bronca em secretário de Guerra por risadas e recebe medalha | G1
articles.standfirst: Guarda chamou a atenção de Pete Hegseth e integrantes da comitiva por causa de comportamento no Túmulo do Soldado Desconhecido. Militar foi condecorado nesta quinta-feira (12).
articles.summary: Guarda chamou a atenção de Pete Hegseth e integrantes da comitiva por causa de comportamento no Túmulo do Soldado Desconhecido. Militar foi condecorado nesta quinta-feira (12).
articles.body:
Um soldado do Exército dos Estados Unidos deu uma bronca no secretário de Guerra, Pete Hegseth, e em integrantes da comitiva dele após ouvir risadas durante uma visita ao Túmulo do Soldado Desconhecido, no Cemitério Nacional de Arlington. O episódio aconteceu na quarta-feira (11). Veja no vídeo acima.

A bronca foi feita durante as comemorações do Dia dos Veteranos nos Estados Unidos, que é um feriado feito para homenagear militares. Um vídeo mostra Hegseth, a mulher dele e assessores tirando fotos e conversando nas escadarias do memorial.

Depois que risadas foram ouvidas, o sentinela Thomas Iglesias se aproximou do grupo e gritou, à distância.

"Todos os visitantes devem manter um ambiente de silêncio e respeito em todos os momentos".

O Túmulo do Soldado Desconhecido é um memorial dedicado a militares americanos mortos em guerras cujos corpos não foram identificados.

Três militares estão enterrados no local, incluindo um que morreu durante a Primeira Guerra Mundial.

Considerado um espaço de homenagem e reflexão sobre o serviço militar, o memorial é protegido por sentinelas do Exército americano 24 horas por dia.

O vídeo viralizou nas redes sociais e foi noticiado na imprensa norte-americana.

O secretário de Guerra dos EUA, Pete Hegseth, durante cerimônia do Dia do Veterano — Foto: Kylie Cooper/Reuters

Após a repercussão, a atitude do militar foi elogiada pelo próprio Pentágono. Em nota, o porta-voz-chefe da pasta, Sean Parnell, afirmou que o secretário e todo o Departamento de Guerra sempre honraram e continuarão honrando os sacrifícios dos militares americanos.

"Durante a comemoração deste dia solene, um soldado lembrou corretamente e de forma respeitosa a todos que mantivessem a compostura", afirmou Parnell.

Nesta quinta-feira (12), Iglesias recebeu a Medalha de Louvor por Serviço Conjunto, uma condecoração concedida pelo desempenho no cumprimento das funções, segundo a imprensa americana.

Hegseth também comentou a premiação nas redes sociais. "Amamos os soldados. Amamos os padrões. Muito bem, especialista. Siga em frente, patriotas", escreveu o secretário.

articles.title: 'Prove it': BJP MLA Maithili Thakur rejects land grabbing allegations against family
articles.summary: BJP MLA Maithili Thakur denies land encroachment allegations against her father, urges complainants to prove claims as officials summon both sides for hearing.
articles.body: PATNA: BJP MLA from Alinagar Maithili Thakur has denied allegations of land encroachment against her father, Ramesh Thakur, and challenged complainants to substantiate their claims before the authorities.Villagers have accused Ramesh of illegally occupying religious sites, govt land, roads and private property. The complaints concern the shrine of Gram Devta Tiwari Baba, a Radha-Krishna temple and a Dihbar. He has also been accused of filling a drainage channel originating from a local pond and constructing a caretaker’s room.Villager Ram Autar Mishra has alleged encroachment on his land, while Ramday Devi claimed excavation along her property’s boundary had endangered trees. Residents have also raised concerns over soil excavation along the boundaries of other private plots.RJD MLA Bhai Virendra accused Maithili’s family of using political influence to grab land. He alleged land grabbing and intimidation had become a pattern among NDA leaders and criticised the media for giving greater prominence to ruling alliance statements than those of the opposition.Rejecting the allegations, Maithili said her family had valid land documents and described the claims circulating on social media over the past two days as baseless. She said a house was being built on land known as ‘Pokhar Bhinda’, where village elders regularly gather and extend their support."I, too, only started seeing these posts two days ago. Land mafias, grabbing land, taking away the poor's rights—I'm reading all these things. These false allegations against our family are baseless. It upsets me deeply to hear that people are writing such things. If there's anything to this, ask the local circle officer. If an allegation is being made, what is it based on? Prove it... I'm very concerned that people are using such strong language—what is it based on?... Baseless rumours are being spread," she said.She urged complainants to approach the circle officer, DCLR or other competent authorities with evidence instead of making allegations online.Circle officer Alok Kumar said an application had been received from villagers and both parties had been summoned to a ‘janata darbar’. articles.title: Mandya woman, for whose ‘murder’ a stranger spent 2.5 years in jail, found alive
articles.summary: Mandya woman missing since 2019 resurfaces alive; Rajesh spent 2.5 years jailed for alleged murder as police probe lapses and torture claims.
articles.body: MANDYA: A Mandya woman presumed murdered seven years ago has resurfaced alive, exposing serious lapses in the investigation that led to a man being charged with her ‘murder’ and jailed for two-and-a-half years.The man, Rajesh, now 36, who secured bail in 2024, has alleged that police tortured him into confessing to a crime he did not commit.Police registered a murder case and arrested Rajesh, relying primarily on the fact that Manju had made her last call borrowing the phone from Rajesh, a stranger, while at a bus stop shortly before she went missing.The case brings back memories of one Suresh from Kodagu, who was similarly accused of ‘murder’ and incarcerated for more than two years following his wife Mallige’s disappearance – until she resurfaced in April 2025.In the current case, Manju, now 36, who went missing from Pandavapura in 2019, was traced in Nagamangala Thursday after Rajesh’s advocate Natesh received a tip-off about her.In her statement to police, Manju reportedly said she had left home voluntarily because her family was forcing her into a marriage against her wishes and had since married another man and settled down. She also said she did not even know Rajesh.Police have initiated a fresh inquiry into her disappearance and the subsequent ‘murder’ probe. Superintendent of police Shobharani confirmed that Manju was placed in a women’s shelter home.Rajesh, a resident of Ragimuddanahalli village in Pandavapura taluk, Mandya, told reporters police inspector Prabhakar subjected him to custodial torture – including electric shocks to his private parts – to extract a confession.Fearing that his family would also be implicated, he claimed, he admitted to the ‘murder’ despite not being involved in it. He remained in prison for nearly two-and-a-half years before securing bail in Feb 2024.The case began in 2019 when Manju’s father, Nagaraju, lodged a missing-person complaint at Pandavapura police station. articles.title: 'Ask him which judges belong to BJP and which to Trinamool', Calcutta HC tells Abhishek Banerjee’s counsel
articles.summary: Calcutta High Court rebukes Trinamool MP Abhishek Banerjee over alleged remarks on judges’ political allegiance as it hears plea against security downgrade.
articles.body: KOLKATA: Trinamool MP Abhishek Banerjee’s alleged comments that “some” high court judges owe allegiance to Bengal’s governing party, made after a reported attack on his Kalighat home last Saturday, prompted Calcutta High Court to tell his lawyer on Thursday, “Your client is very intelligent. Please ask him to give a list of judges who belong to BJP and who belong to Trinamool.”Justice Krishna Rao made the observation after additional advocate general (AAG) Bilwadal Bhattacharyya highlighted Banerjee’s comments, reported in news media, and demanded that criminal contempt proceedings be started against him. Bhattacharya read out Banerjee’s alleged comments on judiciary’s link with the governing party and its impact on verdicts.The MP, whose security cover has been downgraded by the state govt, allegedly made the comments after his house was attacked late on Saturday by around 50 people armed with sticks fitted with nails.Appealing against reduction in Banerjee’s security, his counsel, Shoeb Alam, submitted before Justice Rao, “This is the speech of a man who is exasperated and is running around for your lordship’s protection. Running from pillar to post to get some protection for his family and him, and for no fault of his but because the party he is affiliated with lost elections. Because of which, not one but six attacks have taken place… This is a clear case of breakdown of rule of law.”Justice Rao said, “If you are facing difficulty, court is there. If not this court, then you go to another forum. It (the comment on judiciary’s alleged political link) can be taken if it’s a general public, but if it’s an educated person who is an MP and holding a good post in a political party. He is not a layman who doesn’t know what he is telling before the media. He can say anything against any person. But on a matter pending before the court…”The judge reserved his order on the plea against reduction in Banerjee’s security cover and the subsequent six attacks on him, the latest of which was reported last Saturday. Justice Rao repeatedly asked the state why the six attacks on Banerjee were not taken into account by the govt after the May 29 review meeting, which decided on scaling down his security from Z+ to X.When AAG Bhattacharyya submitted that the threat perception of all MPs would be reassessed at the next review meeting, scheduled for Nov-end, Justice Rao said, “You (the BJP govt) have to wait for six months? Your new regime came on May 10, immediately you reduced. There’s no problem. But once you have received representation (from Banerjee), why are you dragging the matter? Why are you waiting for six months?”Banerjee’s counsel submitted that considering the spate of violence since the announcement of the assembly poll results, his client feared he could be assassinated. He flagged multiple actions by the state, including removal of police kiosks outside Banerjee’s home, and alleged that the govt had acted mala fide.While the MP’s counsel said only two personal security officers had been guarding his client since May 12, the AAG submitted that three PSOs were tasked with protecting Banerjee. He clarified that Z+ security was usually provided to the CM, governor and other persons facing threats. Most MPs, he said, are given X security cover.“Banerjee’s residence continues to remain under high-grade security. He is being provided with three PSOs. Most of the incident petitions are pending. articles.title: Tagged by rivals as BJP’s B team, AIMIM yet to replicate Bihar poll play in UP
articles.summary: AIMIM’s 2027 UP alliance with Azad Samaj Party draws buzz, but the party remains weak in state polls, amid BJP “B team” tag and low vote share.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: When firebrand Hyderabad MP Asaduddin Owaisi’s All India Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) joined hands with Chandrashekhar Azad-led Azad Samaj Party – KanshI Ram (ASP – KR) to contest all 403 UP assembly seats in 2027 polls, the announcement created ripples but failed to trigger any fireworks in the political circles like it did when it entered the Bihar poll fray or the recently concluded West Bengal assembly elections.One reason for this meek entry was that Telangana-headquartered AIMIM has been trying its luck in UP state polls since 2017 UP assembly elections, but has failed to send a single MLA to the state’s Vidhan Sabha in a decade.This has been in sharp contrast to its impactful electoral journey in Bihar and of late even in Maharashtra and West Bengal.Political experts are of the view that more than AIMIM’s political rivals, it is the Muslim community in UP – the core voter base that Owaisi’s party focuses on – which does not see the party as a potential political challenger to national parties like the BJP or the more regionally focused outfits like the Samajwadi Party or the Bahujan Samaj Party for that matter.Lack of organisational machinery and absence of foot soldiers on ground have only compounded Owaisi’s challenges.This apart, another major challenge for the AIMIM in UP is that its political rivals have somewhat successfully managed to label Owaisi as the B team of BJP – a perception that has gained significant ground among Muslims.As a result, while the AIMIM-backed candidates have emerged victorious in local body polls where candidates’ personal relations at the hyper local level matter more than his political affiliations, the party has failed miserably to bag enough votes to put the party candidate in a fighting position.In 2025 Bihar polls, AIMIM contested 29 seats and retained the five that it had won in the Muslim dominated Seemanchal belt in 2020. In 2026 Maharashtra civic polls, Owaisi’s party bagged 114 seats, including 33 in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.In UP, AIMIM started making its presence felt in the run-up to the 2017 assembly polls. The party came under the political spotlight in early 2016 after the then SP govt led by Akhilesh Yadav did not permit Owaisi to address rallies in Azamgarh – a stronghold of SP.Later, Owaisi claimed that he was stopped from visiting the state 12 times and permission to do his rallies were cancelled 28 times in the 12 months before the 2017 polls.The party, however, went on to contest 38 seats in the Assembly polls securing 2,04,142 votes (0.24% of the vote share) without winning a seat.In the 2022 assembly polls, AIMIM contested 96 seats to bag 0.43% vote share. A major political upheaval erupted when it was alleged that AIMIM candidates on many seats secured votes more than BJP’s victory margin.Social media posts then claimed that this happened on 165 seats and Owaisi himself came out in the media to claim that post was unfounded as the party had contested only 96 seats.The 2023 urban bodies elections in UP, however, came as a shot in the arm for the AIMIM with the party’s five chairpersons in the Nagar Palika Parishad and 75 councillors in the municipal corporation making it through.This was a massive increase of 126% in seats from 32 in the previous local body polls. articles.title: Mulheres mais inteligentes são tratadas de forma pior por colegas, aponta estudo | G1
articles.standfirst: Mulheres que obtiveram pontuação mais alta num teste de inteligência foram avaliadas pelos colegas como mais hostis, receberam menos ajuda e foram prejudicadas com mais frequência. Fenômeno não se repete para os homens.
articles.summary: Mulheres que obtiveram pontuação mais alta num teste de inteligência foram avaliadas pelos colegas como mais hostis, receberam menos ajuda e foram prejudicadas com mais frequência. Fenômeno não se repete para os homens.
articles.body:
A inteligência costuma ser considerada um trunfo no trabalho. Mas um novo estudo sugere que, para as mulheres, ela também pode levar a um tratamento pior no ambiente profissional.

Entre 826 pessoas que participaram da pesquisa nos Estados Unidos e na China, mulheres que obtiveram pontuação mais alta num teste de inteligência foram avaliadas pelos colegas de equipe como mais hostis, receberam menos ajuda e foram prejudicadas com mais frequência.

Homens com pontuações altas não receberam esse tratamento ou, então, foram tratados melhor do que outros.

Desde que os resultados foram publicados neste ano, a pesquisadora responsável pelo estudo, Nitya Chawla, da UCL School of Management, em Londres, recebeu mensagens de mulheres que lhe relatavam passar pela mesma experiência no trabalho. Algumas delas, inclusive, disseram que já haviam se perguntado se elas próprias tinham culpa pela hostilidade.

Os pesquisadores realizaram duas rodadas de estudo. A primeira acompanhou 432 estudantes de administração de uma universidade pública dos EUA, que trabalhavam em pequenas equipes num projeto de consultoria para organizações reais.

Já a segunda teve como participantes 394 funcionários em tempo integral, que trabalhavam em equipes numa empresa do ramo financeiro da China.

Na pesquisa, a "inteligência" se equiparava à capacidade cognitiva medida por um teste padronizado de raciocínio e resolução de problemas que os empregadores usam na contratação. Os colegas de equipe não foram informados das pontuações de ninguém.

Os participantes avaliaram uns aos outros e, algumas semanas depois, cada um relatou o quanto havia recebido ajuda e com que frequência havia sido prejudicado, por exemplo, ao ter informações ocultadas.

Ao examinar os resultados, os pesquisadores apontam para a teoria dos papéis sociais. Isto é, a ideia de que as pessoas esperam que homens e mulheres se encaixem em papéis tradicionais: eles como capazes e assertivos, elas como calorosas e solidárias.

Uma mulher com alta capacidade cognitiva quebra essa expectativa, e os colegas podem presumir que ela não é calorosa.

"É essa suposição automática e implícita que ocorre junto com a presença de inteligência que então impulsiona esses comportamentos interpessoais mais negativos", afirma Chawla.

Em ambos os grupos, mulheres com pontuações mais altas foram avaliadas como mais hostis. Entre os funcionários na China, elas também foram avaliadas como menos calorosas. Mulheres vistas como mais hostis relataram ter recebido menos ajuda, tanto no trabalho quanto no plano pessoal, e ser mais prejudicadas.

Os estudiosos também verificaram se as mulheres estavam simplesmente se comportando de maneira diferente.

Aquelas com pontuações mais altas foram avaliadas como um pouco mais dominadoras pelos colegas, mas isso não explicava por que recebiam menos ajuda ou eram pior tratadas. Os resultados apontam para as suposições dos colegas, diz Chawla, e não para algo que as mulheres tenham feito.

Já os homens com pontuações altas de inteligência não enfrentaram o mesmo tratamento.

Entre os estudantes nos Estados Unidos, a pontuação de um homem não fez diferença na forma como seus colegas de equipe o avaliavam ou tratavam.

Já no caso dos funcionários na China, homens com pontuações mais altas foram avaliados como menos hostis, receberam mais ajuda e sofreram menos maus-tratos.

Os autores sugerem que a diferença entre os dois grupos pode refletir diferenças culturais nas normas de gênero, mas não testaram isso.

Chawla coloca a responsabilidade nos locais de trabalho, e não nas mulheres. Sugerir que elas devem esconder sua inteligência seria definitivamente a conclusão errada, ela ressalta.

Cabe aos gestores, diz a pesquisadora, acompanhar como os membros da equipe se tratam. As organizações, por sua vez, devem realizar check-ins regulares para verificar se os funcionários recebem apoio em igual medida.

O estudo, entretanto, tem limitações: a diferença entre homens e mulheres foi pequena. Mas a pesquisadora argumenta que mesmo efeitos pequenos sobre o comportamento importam, porque são vivenciados dia após dia.

"Essas experiências e esses sentimentos podem se tornar muito, muito pesados com o tempo", disse ela.

Com o tempo, ser alvo de tratamento negativo pode levar mulheres a sentirem ansiedade, duvidarem de si mesmas ou nutrirem sensação de não pertencimento.

articles.summary: Moradores de Maragogi e região podem acompanha a programação da TV Globo através do sinal terrestre, além do g1, Globoplay, sinal de tv por assinatura e antenas parabólicas.
articles.body:
Cidade de Maragogi, no Litoral Norte de Alagoas — Foto: Reprodução/TV Asa Branca Alagoas

A TV Asa Branca Alagoas chegou a Maragogi , no Litoral Norte de Alagoas. A partir de agora, os moradores podem acompanhar a programação da TV Globo, com atrações locais e nacionais, pelo canal 28.1, na televisão aberta (veja abaixo como sintonizar).

A expansão do sinal terrestre beneficia cerca de 32 mil habitantes do município, permitindo que a população tenha acesso a conteúdos que reúnem qualidade e credibilidade, características da programação da Globo.

O gerente de tecnologia da TV Asa Branca Alagoas destacou que a emissora passa por um processo de expansão, ampliando sua cobertura para alcançar cada vez mais municípios alagoanos.

“Estamos no sinal terrestre, na antena parabólica, no g1, no streaming, na TV fechada. A estação foi implantada para atender Maragogi e região, que passaram a receber o sinal da TV, reforçando o compromisso de deixar a sociedade alagoana bem informada”, afirmou o gerente Cláudio Oliveira.

Além da expansão do sinal terrestre, uma torre foi instalada no centro de Maragogi, proporcionando imagens do paraíso natural que encanta não apenas os alagoanos, mas também visitantes de diversas partes do mundo.

Os moradores podem assistir à programação local e nacional pelos sinais aberto e fechado de televisão, por streaming no g1 Alagoas, pelo Globoplay, e pelo sinal das antenas parabólicas .

Na programação local, a TV Asa Branca Alagoas conta com os telejornais Jornal da Manhã Alagoas, AB1 e AB2 , além do GE Alagoas , que reúne as principais notícias do esporte.

TV Asa Branca Alagoas chega com sinal aberto de televisão em Maragogi, através do canal 28.1 — Foto: Reprodução/TV Asa Branca Alagoas

Para assistir ao sinal digital, o telespectador precisa de uma antena UHF em boas condições. Antenas antigas, mal instaladas ou com cabos danificados podem prejudicar a recepção, causando imagem travando ou som com falhas.

Além disso, chuvas e ventos fortes podem alterar o direcionamento da antena, exigindo novo ajuste.

Verifique se sua antena é digital (UHF) e está corretamente instalada;

No controle remoto, acesse Menu > Configurações > Canais;

Selecione Busca automática ou Sintonia automática;

Aguarde até que todos os canais sejam encontrados.

Se o sinal continuar instável, é recomendado revisar cabos e conectores ou procurar um técnico especializado em instalação de antenas digitais.

Araruama , na Região dos Lagos do Rio, recebe, entre os dias 17 e 22 de novembro, a 7ª edição do FESTAR — Festival de Teatro de Araruama. O evento reúne 24 grupos teatrais, dos quais três são convidados, com o objetivo de valorizar a produção teatral e o acesso à cultura.

Com o tema “ Minha voz, uso pra dizer o que se cala ”, inspirado na trajetória de Elza Soares, o festival terá apresentações no Teatro Municipal, na Concha Acústica, na Praça João Hélio, e no Espaço Multicultural Gene Insanno (eMGI).

A programação inclui teatro infantil, teatro de rua, teatro alternativo e monólogos, com grupos dos estados do Rio de Janeiro, Rio Grande do Sul, Espírito Santo, Minas Gerais, Paraíba, Santa Catarina e São Paulo.

Além dos espetáculos, o FESTAR contará com atividades formativas e espaços de diálogo entre artistas e público. As apresentações terão tradução em Língua Brasileira de Sinais (Libras).

Outra iniciativa é a publicação de críticas especializadas, assinadas por Lucimar Sena, no site do Gene Insanno, na manhã seguinte a cada apresentação. A proposta é ampliar o debate sobre as obras e valorizar a produção teatral contemporânea.

articles.title: Facções no interior do RJ: grupos armados dominam 21 cidades | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento do g1 com base em dados divulgados pelo Instituto de Segurança Pública mostra presença de facções no interior do Rio.
articles.summary: Levantamento inédito mostra que facções no interior do RJ diversificaram atividades e já impõem regras em 21 municípios com menos de 30 mil habitantes.
articles.body:
Fenômeno geralmente associado às grandes cidades e regiões metropolitanas, o domínio armado de territórios também já está presente em cidades pequenas do estado do Rio .

Um levantamento do g1 com base em dados divulgados pelo Instituto de Segurança Pública (ISP) mostra que 21 cidades com menos menos de 30 mil habitantes , segundo Censo do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), já registram a presença de grupos criminosos armados.

Na divisa com o estado de Minas Gerais, a pequena cidade de Comendador Levy Gasparian , com 8,7 mil habitantes segundo o Censo 2022, é a menor do estado do Rio de Janeiro a ter a presença de organizações criminosas, segundo o levantamento.

Mapa do ISP mostra o controle dos territórios do RJ por organizações criminosas — Foto: Arte/g1

Na Região Serrana, Trajano de Moraes , com pouco mais de 10 mil moradores, também tem uma área dominada pela maior facção criminosa do estado.

Nos dois casos, a presença ainda é pequena, com menos de 1% da área total do município com a presença dessas organizações.

No grupo das cidades com menos de 30 mil habitantes, a que tem maior presença percentual de facções é Porto Real , no Médio Paraíba. Com 20 mil moradores, a cidade tem, segundo o ISP, 4% de seu território com presença de organizações armadas.

Para a socióloga Roberta Fernandes, pesquisadora do Centro de Estudos de Criminalidade e Segurança Pública da Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (Crisp/UFMG), o mapeamento mostra a mudança no perfil das facções criminosas.

"A gente percebe que essas organizações hoje elas não dependem exclusivamente do uso da questão do tráfico de drogas. Muito pelo contrário. Há estudos que mostram que a questão do tráfico de droga tá ali em terceiro, quarto lugar. Eles diversificaram as atividades de tal forma que eles que eles passaram a explorar outros mercados", explica.

"A gente tem que lembrar que existem outras regulações dentro desses territórios estabelecidos pelo proceder dessas organizações, como, por exemplo, toque de recolher, as questões econômicas de mercado. Quem vende, quem pode vender, o que pode vender?", completa.

articles.summary: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to bring European nations into the next round of peace negotiations, US President Donald Trump's envoy and son-in-law Jared
articles.body: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to bring European nations into the next round of peace negotiations, US President Donald Trump's envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner said on Thursday, as Washington pushes for what could become the war's "largest prisoner exchange".Kushner said the expanded format would give negotiators an opportunity to discuss wider European security concerns along with the territorial dispute between Moscow and Kyiv."We are also working toward what would be the largest prisoner exchange of the war, potentially reuniting thousands of people with their families," Kushner wrote on X, without disclosing details of the proposed arrangement.He said the US was encouraged by the movement in negotiations, although substantial differences between the two sides continued to stand in the way of a settlement.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also welcomed the possibility of European countries joining the next round of US-led discussions. After meeting US envoys Steve Witkoff and Kushner, he said the resumption of diplomatic engagement was significant and voiced hope that the discussions would address ceasefire efforts and ways to ease the conflict.The Abu Dhabi meeting earlier this week marked the first round of talks between the sides in nine months.Witkoff had earlier said Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to European representatives joining the upcoming negotiations. Putin, however, also called on Washington to engage with its European allies to determine whether they were seeking peace or war in Ukraine.Kushner and Witkoff held separate engagements with the two leaders, travelling to Moscow for a meeting with Putin before heading to Dublin for talks with Zelenskyy.Kushner said any sustainable agreement would need credible security guarantees and "reciprocal" commitments to de-escalate tensions to prevent another conflict.However, territorial disagreements remain a major stumbling block. Russia controls roughly a fifth of Ukrainian territory, while Kyiv has ruled out surrendering the remaining parts of the eastern Donbas region.Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Trump returned to the White House promising to end the war but has so far been unable to broker an agreement.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Whoop launches ‘Humans,’ a social network it says is built on verified heartbeats
articles.summary: Whoop, the fitness and wearable maker has launched Humans, a social network inside its app that it pitches as free of bots and AI-generated content as
articles.body: Whoop, the fitness and wearable maker has launched Humans, a social network inside its app that it pitches as free of bots and AI-generated content as every account belongs to a real person wearing its tracker. The company started rolling out the functionality for its members starting November 12. The company claims that Whoop Humans allow the members to follow friends and family and share their sleep, recovery, strain workouts and achievements. The company has also made it clear that it is not a place for text status updates. Users can also select which health metrics they want to share with their friends and family. The members can also manage their followers and remove people from their network. Along with this, they can also select which workout types and achievements appear, and keep personal photos and ‘moments’ private.The ‘human’ pitchWhoop mentioned that all the accounts present on the platform are of real persons and are verified with a heartbeat. The company class the service ‘the most verifiably human network ever.’ The company further added that the legacy social media is increasingly saturated with AI, automated accounts and manufactured content. The company bases that claim on the fact that every post is backed by physiological data. Whoop also says Humans is designed to show that greater connection and stronger privacy can coexist.Whoop Humans also introduces Moments, allowing members to share photos from workouts, personal milestones, and meaningful experiences. By bringing the stories behind the data into the WHOOP experience, Moments helps members celebrate not just the numbers, but the lives and achievements they represent. Members can also choose to keep Moments private.Privacy at its coreWHOOP Humans is designed to make meaningful connections possible without compromising personal privacy. Members control what health and performance information they share, who can see it, and when they want to remain private.Key privacy protections include:•Granular health data controls: Members choose which metrics to share, including Recovery, Strain, Sleep, HRV, and resting heart rate.•Control over connections: Members can manage their followers and remove individuals from their WHOOP Humans network.•Stealth Mode: Members can temporarily hide their shared health and performance information without changing their sharing preferences.•Sensitive activity protections: Activities designated as sensitive are not shared by default.•Selective activity and achievement sharing: Members choose which workout types and achievements appear in WHOOP Humans.•Private Moments: Members can keep personal photos and Moments private rather than sharing them with their network.•Ongoing privacy management: Members can update their sharing preferences at any time.Your child uses AI every day. articles.title: A man lost a woman's phone number after meeting her at a Leeds nightclub in 1970; he returned to the same club, found her again and married her a year later
articles.summary: A man who lost a woman's phone number after meeting her at a nightclub in Leeds returned to the same venue in the hope of finding her again.
articles.body: A man who lost a woman's phone number after meeting her at a nightclub in Leeds returned to the same venue in the hope of finding her again. Terry Kirwin, then 31, had met Patricia Anne Kirwin, 24, in 1970 but had no way of contacting her after losing her number. His return to the nightclub gave him another chance to ask her out, and the pair went on to marry in August 1971. In October 2026, the couple celebrated 55 years of marriage, sharing their story and advice for a lasting relationship through Care UK's Weavers Court care home.How did a man meet his future wife at a Leeds nightclub in 1970The couple's first meeting took place at a nightclub in Kirkstall, Leeds, in 1970. After losing Pat's number, Terry decided to revisit the venue where they had first met. His return eventually gave him another opportunity to speak to her and ask her out.According to Care UK, Terry was finally able to arrange their first official date, during which the pair spent hours chatting and getting to know one another at a pub. Their initial meeting at the nightclub thus marked the beginning of a relationship that would lead to marriage the following year.After meeting in 1970, Pat and Terry married within a year. The wedding took place at St Peter's Church in Belle Isle on a sunny day in August 1971. The couple celebrated their marriage with a traditional, large church wedding, followed by a buffet reception at the local pub, The Halfway House. Their wedding marked the beginning of their married life together, which they celebrated reaching its 55th anniversary in October 2026.What is the secret to Pat and Terry's 55-year marriageWhen asked about the secret to a long and successful marriage, Terry highlighted the importance of enjoying life together and maintaining honesty. He said: "Good fun and lots of laughs, along with honesty!"Pat and Terry also shared three pieces of advice for younger couples looking to build lasting relationships. Their recommendations were to "pick the right person, commitment from both people, and stay honest".How many children and grandchildren do Pat and Terry havePatricia Anne Kirwin is a resident at Care UK's Weavers Court care home on Naylor Avenue in Yeadon, where the couple marked their 55th wedding anniversary. The celebration recognised their milestone and provided an opportunity to reflect on the years they have spent together.Pat and Terry have two children, Richard and Joanne, and two grandchildren, Thomas and Samuel. The couple continue to spend time with their family while cherishing the memories and experiences they have shared throughout their life together.Sarah Kunica, Home Manager at Weavers Court, also spoke about the significance of the occasion and the couple's relationship. She said: "It was extra special celebrating the love between Pat and Terry. Their devotion to one another is a beautiful example of long-lasting love and commitment."She added that celebrating important milestones and making special occasions memorable for residents was an important part of life at the care home. Reflecting on the couple's anniversary, Kunica said: "It was truly a privilege to listen to the memories and wisdom Pat and Terry shared with us – happy 55th anniversary to you both!"You use AI every day. articles.summary: BENGALURU: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit Bengaluru on Friday to inaugurate the Namma Metro Pink Line and attend the Golden Jubilee
articles.body: BENGALURU: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit Bengaluru on Friday to inaugurate the Namma Metro Pink Line and attend the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram, which also mark the birth centenary of author HV Sheshadri.The programme at S-VYASA University, organised by the S-VYASA Registered Society, is scheduled to begin at 10am. RSS Sarkaryavah Dattatreya Hosabale will attend as the distinguished guest, while Karnataka governor Sudha Yadav, chief minister DK Shivakumar and Ahn Byeong-Gu, mayor of South Korea's Miryang City, will be guests of honour.The celebrations mark 50 years of Prashanti Kutiram, which is known for its work in yoga research. H.R. Nagendra, president of VYASA Society, said the institution was developing a specialised research laboratory, named Ritambhara, to study higher dimensions of yoga, including Samadhi."We are celebrating the Golden Jubilee of 50 years of our service at Prashanti Kutiram. We are known for research in the world. We are going further to develop the most unique research lab called Ritambhara to track the higher dimensions of yoga to what we call Samadhi," Nagendra told news agency ANI.He also announced the launch of S-VYASA's Thiruvananthapuram campus to coincide with the Prime Minister's visit. Nagendra acknowledged the contributions of the institution's faculty, students and alumni and invited people to join the celebrations online.Meanwhile, the institution will organise a free artificial limb fitting camp to commemorate Sheshadri's birth centenary. Prem Bhandari, chief adviser for international affairs at S-VYASA, said 1,000 people would be provided with artificial limbs under the initiative.Bhandari, who represents Jaipur Foot USA, said the decision was taken after discussions with the organisation's founder, Padma Bhushan D.R. Mehta.He also recalled Modi's association with the initiative, saying the Prime Minister had inaugurated one of its camps in 2016 at his request.Bhandari said he was also working towards establishing an S-VYASA centre in New York, as part of efforts to expand the institution's international presence.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan buy 440-acre Irish estate for about $57 million, featuring a Gothic castle, 16,000-square-foot mansion, historic architecture and stunning River Blackwater views
articles.summary: A historic Irish estate has become the latest addition to Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan’s growing property portfolio.
articles.body: A historic Irish estate has become the latest addition to Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan’s growing property portfolio. The Meta chief executive and his wife have purchased Strancally Castle, a sprawling 440-acre property in County Waterford, Ireland, featuring a Gothic-style mansion overlooking the River Blackwater. The acquisition brings a 19th-century residence, with a history stretching back nearly 200 years, into the family’s collection of homes.As reported by the Irish Times, dated October 7, 2026, the purchase price was initially estimated at between €20 million and €30 million. However, Ireland's Property Price Register subsequently recorded a sale figure of €51.17 million for the property, covering the principal residence and up to one acre of land. The total expenditure on the full estate is understood to be higher.Inside Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan’s 440-acre Irish estate and Gothic castleStrancally Castle sits on an extensive stretch of land in County Waterford, with the main residence occupying around 16,000 square feet. Strancally Castle is a three-storey Gothic Revival mansion spanning approximately 16,000 square feet, set within a 440-acre estate overlooking the River Blackwater. Its position overlooking the River Blackwater gives the property a distinctive setting in the Irish countryside.The house has undergone renovation work over the past two decades, bringing changes to a building that dates back to around 1830. Its original construction was commissioned by John Keily, a former member of the British Parliament. Irish architects James and George Richard Pain were responsible for its design. The brothers also worked on several other historic buildings in Ireland, including castle residences.The scale of the estate extends well beyond the main house. Its extensive grounds and historic architecture distinguish it from a conventional luxury residential purchase.Mark Zuckerberg’s Irish castle purchase price and previous ownersThe purchase price was subsequently disclosed through Ireland's Property Price Register. According to the Irish Times, Zuckerberg and Chan paid €51,171,155 for Strancally Castle, with the sale recorded on August 17, 2026. The registered figure covers the principal residence and up to one acre of land, meaning the couple's total expenditure on the entire 440-acre estate would be considerably higher.The estate was previously owned by Michael Alen-Buckley, co-founder of investment management firm RAB Capital, and his wife, Giancarla Alen-Buckley. The couple expressed their happiness at the change in ownership in a statement to the Irish Times, saying, “We leave our home of 25 years fondly and are grateful for the opportunity we have been given to save and restore Strancally Castle ... We are delighted that Mark and his family intend to build on our stewardship by continuing to invest in maintaining and enhancing the property and grounds as their home in a sustainable manner ... We wish them and their family much happiness in this unique and blessed place.”Zuckerberg's spokesperson Brian Baker also confirmed the purchase. He said, “Mark and his family look forward to caring for this historic home and visiting when traveling to Ireland, where Meta maintains its international headquarters.”Why Mark Zuckerberg chose Ireland for his latest property purchaseThe location has a connection to Zuckerberg's professional life as well as his family's property interests. Ireland is home to Meta's European headquarters, which the company established in the country in 2009. Its substantial Irish operations make the country a destination for Zuckerberg's business-related visits.The company, which operates Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, has maintained a substantial presence in Ireland for years. The castle is therefore expected to serve as a place for the family to stay when visiting the country rather than simply another overseas property.The purchase also places the couple among wealthy technology executives who have acquired substantial residential properties outside the United States. Their latest acquisition is considerably different from the modern homes and large residential compounds more commonly associated with Silicon Valley fortunes.Zuckerberg's property portfolio stretches across several US statesStrancally Castle is far from the first major property purchase made by Zuckerberg and Chan. The couple have built up an extensive collection of residential properties, with holdings in California, Hawaii and other parts of the United States.In Palo Alto, California, Zuckerberg reportedly spent more than $110 million acquiring at least 11 properties in the affluent Crescent Park neighbourhood. The purchases attracted attention from local residents as several homes in the area became part of his wider property holdings.He also previously owned a San Francisco residence, which he sold in 2022 for $31 million. In Washington, DC, the Meta founder paid approximately $23 million in cash for a mansion spanning around 15,000 square feet.Hawaii is another important part of the family's real estate interests. Zuckerberg has invested in a large property there, while Lake Tahoe is home to another sizable compound associated with the technology executive. His interest in water sports has also been visible on social media, where he has shared footage of himself hydrofoiling.The Irish castle adds a different kind of property to this collection, bringing historic European architecture into a portfolio otherwise centred largely on American residential estates.Mark Zuckerberg’s growing property portfolio and interest in classical historyZuckerberg's interest in classical history has occasionally appeared in his personal life. He and Chan have given their daughters names associated with Roman history, reflecting an interest in the ancient world, as reported by Los Angeles Times.Strancally Castle, with its 19th-century origins and Gothic architecture, offers another connection to European history. Its previous owners have expressed their hope that the property will remain well maintained under the family's ownership.Zuckerberg, who leads Meta, had an estimated fortune of more than $200 billion, according to Bloomberg's Billionaires Index in November 2026. The acquisition of the Waterford estate adds another substantial property to the family's holdings.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available reports and property records. The Times of India has not independently verified the transaction details, property valuation or total purchase price of the estate.Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? articles.title: Amid Nvidia scandal, Trump, Xi, Putin to share APEC stage in China: 5 key issues to watch
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are among the world leaders expected to attend the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are among the world leaders expected to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China's southern technology hub of Shenzhen on November 18 and 19. The gathering comes at a time of growing geopolitical tensions, trade uncertainties and competition over technology, with the possible interaction between the three leaders expected to draw particular attention.The summit will bring together leaders of 21 APEC member economies, which collectively account for approximately 62% of global GDP and around half of global trade. While economic cooperation remains the forum's primary objective, the presence of leaders from three major global powers has added a strategic dimension to this year's meeting.From the Russia-Ukraine war and nuclear disarmament to US-China trade tensions and disputes in the Indo-Pacific, several issues could shape the discussions on the sidelines of the summit.Here are five key issues that make the China-hosted APEC summit important.1. Trump-Xi-Putin dynamics: Nuclear disarmament and global securityThe possible presence of Trump, Xi and Putin at the same gathering has put their diplomatic interactions under the spotlight. The three countries have overlapping interests in global security, nuclear weapons and international stability, but their strategic priorities often differ.One of the major issues is nuclear disarmament. The US and Russia possess considerably larger nuclear arsenals than China, which has been reluctant to participate in trilateral arms control negotiations.According to analysts, Beijing is hesitant to engage in nuclear disarmament discussions with Washington and Moscow because of the disparity in their nuclear capabilities. China maintains that negotiations should take into account the differences between the countries' respective arsenals.The summit could provide an opportunity for informal exchanges on strategic stability, although APEC itself is primarily an economic forum and does not have a mandate to negotiate nuclear arms control agreements.2. Russia-Ukraine war: Will Trump and Putin discuss the conflict?The Russia-Ukraine war is another major issue that could feature in discussions between Trump and Putin.Washington and Moscow have a direct interest in the conflict, particularly over the prospects of ending hostilities and the future security arrangements in Europe.The presence of Xi adds another dimension to the diplomatic equation. China maintains close strategic and economic ties with Russia, while also seeking to position itself as an influential player in international diplomacy.However, analysts suggest that discussions between the US and Russia on Ukraine may not necessarily involve China.Any interaction between Trump and Putin could attract attention for indications of their respective positions on the conflict, negotiations and the broader relationship between Washington and Moscow.3. US-China trade tensions: Tariffs, rare earths and AIRelations between Washington and Beijing will be among the most closely watched aspects of the summit.The two countries have been attempting to maintain a trade truce, but analysts say both sides are falling short of commitments to an extended agreement.Trade restrictions, tariffs and access to critical minerals remain key areas of disagreement.Rare earth supplies are particularly important because China occupies a dominant position in the global processing and supply chain for these materials. They are essential for manufacturing electric vehicles, electronics, defence equipment and several advanced technologies.Artificial intelligence is another potential area of discussion. Both countries are competing for leadership in advanced computing, semiconductor technology and AI development.The US restrictions on advanced chip exports to China and Beijing's efforts to strengthen its domestic semiconductor industry have added to the technology rivalry.US arms sales to Taiwan could also emerge as a contentious issue. Beijing opposes American military support for the island, which it considers part of its territory, while Washington maintains its commitments to Taiwan's defence capabilities.4. China-Japan tensions: Taiwan emerges as a flashpointRelations between China and Japan are another important issue to watch at the summit.Tensions between the two countries have persisted since November 2025, when Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi angered Beijing by suggesting that Japan could deploy its military if a Chinese move against neighbouring Taiwan also threatened Japanese territory.The remarks added to existing disagreements over Taiwan and regional security.China considers Taiwan part of its territory and has not ruled out the use of force to achieve reunification. Japan, meanwhile, views stability in the Taiwan Strait as important to its national security, given its geographical proximity to the island.Any interaction between Chinese and Japanese representatives at the summit could offer an indication of whether the two sides are willing to manage their differences through diplomatic engagement.However, Tokyo has not formally confirmed whether Takaichi will attend the meeting.5. South China Sea and Middle East instability: Trade and energy security at stakeRegional maritime disputes and instability in the Middle East are also expected to feature in discussions among APEC economies.China and the Philippines continue to face tensions over competing territorial claims and maritime activities in the South China Sea. The strategic waterway is an important international shipping route, carrying a substantial share of global trade.The participation of Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. will bring additional attention to the maritime disputes and the broader question of regional security.Meanwhile, instability in the Middle East poses risks to energy supplies, shipping routes and international supply chains.Disruptions to maritime traffic and energy exports could increase transportation costs, push up fuel prices and add to inflationary pressures across economies.For several Asia-Pacific countries that depend heavily on imported energy and international trade, maintaining stable shipping routes and securing energy supplies remain important economic priorities.What is APEC and who are its members?Established in 1989 in Canberra, Australia, APEC began as an informal dialogue involving 12 economies. It has since developed into one of the region's leading platforms for economic cooperation, trade and investment.The forum currently has 21 member economies: Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Peru, the Philippines, Russia, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand, the United States and Vietnam.APEC uses the term "member economies" rather than countries, allowing participation by territories with different political and administrative arrangements, including Hong Kong and Taiwan.Its decisions are based on consensus and are non-binding, with members undertaking commitments voluntarily.Despite being the world's most populous country and a major Indo-Pacific economy, India is not a member of APEC.Why is Shenzhen hosting the summit?China is hosting the APEC summit for the third time, following earlier meetings in Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014.Shenzhen, located in southern China near Hong Kong, is a major technology and manufacturing centre. It is home to several prominent Chinese companies, including electric vehicle maker BYD, telecommunications company Huawei and technology giant Tencent.The city is also part of China's Greater Bay Area, which includes Hong Kong, Macau and several cities in Guangdong province. Beijing aims to develop the region into a global hub for technology, innovation and finance.According to Chim Lee, senior analyst at the Economist Intelligence Unit, the choice of Shenzhen reflects both domestic and international considerations.The summit provides China an opportunity to showcase its economic development, technological capabilities and ambitions in global trade, while demonstrating the city's resilience amid geopolitical tensions.With Trump, Xi and Putin among the expected participants, the Shenzhen gathering will be watched not only for economic commitments but also for the diplomatic signals emerging from interactions between some of the world's most influential leaders.You use AI every day. articles.title: Railways looking into eliminating RAC for train journey
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Railways is looking into the option of doing away with the Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) facility, under which two passengers are
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Railways is looking into the option of doing away with the Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) facility, under which two passengers are allotted a single berth and charged the full fare despite getting only half the sleeping space.TOI has learnt that the move is being examined in the wake of concerns over passenger convenience and the need to revisit a provision that has remained part of the reservation system for decades. “There is a view that when a passenger isn’t getting full sleeping space, it may not be appropriate to charge the full fare,” said an official.The RAC facility also becomes a cause for discomfort when the same seat is allotted to a male and a female passenger. Train ticket examiners face challenges in finding an alternative arrangement in such cases.The issue of travelers with RAC tickets being charged full fares has also been flagged by a parliamentary panel, which questioned its rationale. The panel has recommended that railways review the existing arrangement to ensure passengers are not made to pay the full fare without getting the benefit of a proper berth.RAC was introduced when railway ticket reservations were largely handled manually, and there was no electronic system to dynamically track cancellations and vacant berths. The arrangement allowed two passengers to travel on a single berth, with the possibility of one getting a full berth if another passenger cancelled their ticket.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2024, Montana-born photographer Arnold Swanberg died after leaving 480 acres of farmland to a research institute; in 2026, the $1 million gift is supporting Alzheimer's research in his hometown
articles.summary: A Montana-born photographer who spent much of his adult life in Seattle has left behind an unusual legacy, 480 acres of farmland worth an estimated $1
articles.body: A Montana-born photographer who spent much of his adult life in Seattle has left behind an unusual legacy, 480 acres of farmland worth an estimated $1 million, now earmarked to support Alzheimer's research in his hometown. According to an announcement by the Weissman Hood Institute, Arnold Swanberg, who died in October 2024, bequeathed two parcels of agricultural land to the research institute in Great Falls, Montana. In 2026, the donation is drawing attention for the role it could play in advancing research into Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and other neurodegenerative diseases.Swanberg's will reportedly specified that the land should be held as an endowment to fund Alzheimer's research, ensuring that the farmland would continue contributing to the community long after his death. The institute estimates the combined value of the two parcels at approximately $1 million, making it one of the largest donations in its history.Why did Swanberg leave his farmland to a research institute?Born in Great Falls in 1948, Swanberg spent most of his adult life in Seattle, Washington. However, he maintained a strong connection to Montana, particularly through the agricultural properties he had inherited. The two parcels are located in different parts of the state: one south of the Great Falls airport in Cascade County and another in Teton County, north of Benton Lake. Not a farmer himself, Swanberg leased the properties to local agricultural workers. Over the years, he developed friendships with the people who cultivated the land and continued visiting Montana twice annually, usually in spring and autumn, to check on the properties.His decision to leave the farmland to the Weissman Hood Institute was also influenced by personal experiences with neurodegenerative diseases. According to Randy Gray, a former Great Falls mayor and one of Swanberg's closest friends, the photographer had witnessed the impact of these conditions within his family. Speaking to KRTV, Gray explained that Swanberg's family had a history of neurodegenerative diseases, giving him a personal reason to support research in this area.The institute's official announcement also noted that Swanberg wanted his inherited Montana land to benefit the state over the long term. Gray recalled that Swanberg had discussed his estate planning with him and expressed a desire to ensure that the property continued serving Montana.From military aircraft photography to supporting medical researchSwanberg's life followed a different path from that of his family's three generations of lawyers in Great Falls. After graduating from the University of Montana with a history degree in 1970, he served in the Montana Air National Guard before moving to Seattle. His military service sparked a lifelong fascination with aviation, which eventually developed into an ambitious photography project. He travelled internationally, photographing military aircraft and attempting to document aircraft tail numbers from every unit of the US military.Swanberg also managed his family's real estate investments and published a military aviation magazine called Flight Line, which covered military aircraft around the world. His photography collection eventually became part of the Museum of Flight in Seattle. He also supported his former university by establishing an annual lecture in military history.Despite building his professional life elsewhere, Montana remained important to him. The land donation reflected that continuing connection and his interest in ensuring that scientific research could benefit people in the state where he grew up.How will the $1 million farmland donation support Alzheimer's research?The 480 acres will not be converted into laboratories or research facilities immediately. Instead, the farmland will continue to be leased to local farmers, with the proceeds directed towards Alzheimer's research at the institute's Center for Integrated Biomedical and Rural Health Research (CIB-RHR). The arrangement will allow the institute to preserve the agricultural use of the properties while generating a continuing source of financial support for scientific work.According to the institute, the endowment will provide researchers with greater financial flexibility, allowing them to pursue projects that may otherwise struggle to secure funding. The donation also comes at a significant time for medical research in Montana. The CIB-RHR was established through a partnership involving the Weissman Hood Institute, Touro College of Osteopathic Medicine-Montana and Benefis Health System. Supported by funding from the National Institutes of Health, the centre focuses on bringing biomedical and clinical research to rural communities. Its research interests include Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, age-related vision loss and chronic wasting disease in deer.The need for such research is particularly relevant in Montana, where the Alzheimer's Association estimates that approximately 21,000 residents over the age of 65 are living with Alzheimer's disease. The state also faces a shortage of dementia specialists, making access to research and medical expertise an important concern.Could the farmland itself become part of scientific research?Swanberg's donation could eventually contribute to research beyond its financial value. Scientists are increasingly interested in understanding whether agricultural environments and occupational exposures could influence the risk of developing neurodegenerative diseases.Farmers, for instance, have been found to face an increased risk of Parkinson's disease in some studies. Researchers have been investigating whether repeated exposure to agricultural chemicals, including herbicides and pesticides, could be among the contributing factors.Gray told KRTV that Swanberg's farmland could potentially become a test site for research examining such connections. The institute is also exploring the relationship between genetics, lifestyle and neurological conditions among people living in rural environments. The research could help scientists understand whether environmental factors influence the development of diseases such as Parkinson's and Alzheimer's.For now, the properties will remain agricultural land, with the farmers who have worked there continuing their activities. Their lease payments will help support the institute's research priorities.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Europe plans to heat 6,500 homes and a school using crematorium heat; how the unusual energy recycling system works
articles.summary: In 2011, Redditch Borough Council in England decided to experiment with something that hardly anyone in the UK had heard of before.
articles.body: In 2011, Redditch Borough Council in England decided to experiment with something that hardly anyone in the UK had heard of before. Staff announced they were going to warm the local swimming pool with heat from a nearby crematorium. What ensued was a public firestorm with the plan making international headlines and even gaining criticism locally. Eventually, the project proved to be one of the most thoughtful decisions, winning a green award. Since 2013, the crematorium has warmed Redditch's swimming pool, as per a report by WIRED.European countries have been harvesting warmth from crematoriums for years. The total volume of heat available from the crematoriums is modest, but with an increasing search for ways of reducing the environmental impact of funeral rites, utilising this heat provides a way to lower their carbon intensity.Roughly 1,200 cremations are carried out every year in Redditch. A heat exchanger captures heat from flue gases emitted by the facility’s two gas-fired ovens as part of a process to remove vaporised mercury from dental fillings, before venting the remaining gas into the atmosphere. In Redditch, the heat exchanger connects to a water loop that travels 200 meters underground, eventually reaching another heat exchanger supplying the swimming pool.Helpfully, such a sizable body of water “acts as a heat sink”, said Guy Revans, of Redditch and Bromsgrove Councils. “You put heat into it during the day; it retains that heat for a considerable length of time.” The recreation centre also has gas-fired boilers that can provide more heat when necessary. Overall, the system has saved the council tens of thousands of pounds per year in fuel costs.Not just swimming pools, a school currently under construction in Aberdeen, Scotland, will receive excess heat from the city's crematorium. The crematorium already relies on waste heat to warm its own premises. “They were only utilising a tiny amount of the heat available; the rest was going to the atmosphere,” said Ian Davidson, chief executive of Aberdeen Heat & Power, who said that the system now has full planning permission. The crematorium will provide just under 1 gigawatt-hour of heat annually, roughly half the school’s total requirement. A heat pump will cover the rest of the facility’s needs, and the entire system should be fully operational by February 2027.In Finland, the crematorium set to open in Kangasala in 2028 will be connected to the town's district heat network, a system of pipes that supplies more than 6,500 homes with hot water for heating. The crematorium will be fully electric, powered partly by solar panels on its roof. “It’s a special thing,” said Timo Heikkilä, an energy and building systems consultant at Thenco Oy, who is working on the project. “I’m really glad I get to be a part of this.” Winter temperatures in Kangasala can remain below 0 degrees Celsius for weeks on end. In Finland, there is a push to use less natural gas for heating, added Heikkilä.Ian Rudkin, who has managed multiple crematoria in the UK and is currently a board member of the Cremation Society of Great Britain, said many crematoria are becoming more eco-conscious. Some crematoria hold coffins for up to 72 hours, so that several may be cremated in a sequence, making it more efficient. “When we first brought that in, [families] seemed a little bit shocked,” said Rudkin. Soon, however, people became more accepting.Recovering heat from cremations is one way of attempting to counter the “devastating impact” that humans have had on the environment, said Hannah Rumble, an associate at the University of Bath’s Centre for Death and Society. “I can see that would be a reason why people might choose to be cremated at a particular crematorium.”A study published in the journal Energy in 2024 estimated that, if all crematoria in the UK were tapped for waste heat, they might only meet 1 per cent of the country’s total heating needs. While it sounds small, decarbonising heat is notoriously difficult, so any interventions to achieve that can be valuable.“I have thought about it, and once my time is up, I would like to be cremated, and I would like my waste heat to be recycled,” shared Heikkilä. “It’s the sensible thing. The last favour you can do for the world.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Massachusetts woman turned a beach-inspired idea into a $1 million handmade charm necklace business in six months, after a TikTok video featuring an influencer brought her brand millions of views
articles.summary: A search for a charm necklace before a holiday helped turn Kelly Bozigian's beachside idea into a rapidly growing jewellery business.
articles.body: A search for a charm necklace before a holiday helped turn Kelly Bozigian's beachside idea into a rapidly growing jewellery business. The Massachusetts entrepreneur launched Coastal Caviar in January 2024, offering handmade charm necklaces and an online experience that allowed customers to design their own pieces. Within six months, the company had crossed $1 million in sales without paid advertising. What began as a hobby alongside a corporate job soon became a full-time venture, fuelled by social media attention, personalised products and a growing customer base.Beach-inspired jewellery idea became a million-dollar businessThe idea for Coastal Caviar came to Bozigian in June 2023 while she was at the beach with her family. As reported by Entrepreneur, she was looking online for a charm necklace to wear on an upcoming holiday and struggled to find mainstream retailers offering the style she wanted.She eventually ordered a necklace from an Etsy seller, but the process involved screenshots, messages and several exchanges to finalise the design. The experience left her thinking there had to be a simpler way for customers to create jewellery they actually wanted.Rather than focusing only on selling necklaces, Bozigian imagined an interactive website where shoppers could select charms, arrange them and see their designs take shape in real time. This idea became the foundation of Coastal Caviar.A business built around personalisationThe company launched in January 2024, with Bozigian initially making the necklaces herself. Entrepreneur reported that she began developing the business after purchasing a domain name and working on the website soon after the original idea came to her.Its online charm builder gave customers a more convenient way to personalise jewellery. Instead of exchanging messages with a seller to explain their preferences, shoppers could put together their own combinations.The beach-inspired designs also helped establish the brand's identity. Coastal Caviar offered charm necklaces and bracelets, with pieces reflecting the coastal aesthetic that Bozigian wanted to bring into the business.Her husband, Colt, continued working in software sales while helping her with the venture. Bozigian herself initially managed the company alongside her corporate job as an associate creative director at TJX Companies, working on the TJ Maxx brand.How did social media change the businessThe turning point arrived shortly after the business launched. Entrepreneur reported that Bozigian began a TikTok series in which she made charm necklaces for influencers. One of her videos featured a necklace created for Alix Earle, an influencer she admired.Earle noticed the video and asked Bozigian to send her the necklace. Bozigian and her husband filmed her reaction to receiving the message and shared it online.The reaction video attracted more than two million views, while Earle's own video featuring the necklace received over nine million views, according to Entrepreneur.The exposure quickly translated into orders. In its first month, Coastal Caviar recorded more than $100,000 in sales, with TikTok playing a major role in bringing customers to the business.CBS Boston's October 2024 report described how a necklace made by Bozigian appeared in a People Magazine article featuring Earle and Taylor Swift at a playoff game. That visibility helped bring in a surge of custom jewellery orders, with the business receiving as many as 300 orders in a single day.From a living room operation to a growing brandThe sudden popularity presented a challenge for the couple. Bozigian was still making necklaces by hand, and the volume of orders quickly exceeded what she had anticipated.Entrepreneur reported that she had to work through nights to fulfil orders during the early days. Three months after the launch, the company moved to a manufacturer in Rhode Island, helping ease the pressure of producing every necklace herself.By then, the business had already reached a remarkable milestone. Within six months of launching, Coastal Caviar had generated $1 million in sales without spending money on paid advertising.The growth eventually allowed Bozigian to leave her corporate job. The company also began moving beyond online sales. Its Boston Seaport pop-up, called the Caviar Bar, offered customers the opportunity to create custom necklaces and other jewellery in person. CBS Boston reported that shoppers could also design bag charms, reflecting the company's efforts to extend its personalisation concept into new products.A trademark dispute led to another unexpected chapterThe business encountered a significant setback when a trademark lawsuit forced it to change its name. According to Sent News, jewellery company Lagos, which was founded in 1977, held a federal trademark covering its caviar line and challenged Coastal Caviar's use of the word.The dispute arrived at an especially difficult moment. Bozigian and her husband had signed a 3-year lease for a new flagship store in Charleston, South Carolina, and the original brand name had already been printed on signs, bags and packaging.Sent News reported that the couple initially planned to fight the lawsuit but later realised they could not afford to take the case to trial. They announced the new name, Club Coastal, on April 19, while racing to replace the branding ahead of the store's opening.The rebranding became another major social media moment. Bozigian shared the uncertainty and preparations with followers, allowing them to watch the business navigate the situation.The rebrand became a sales milestoneThe name change did not slow the business down. Sent News reported that Club Coastal's TikTok following grew from around 80,000 to nearly 125,000 during the roughly six weeks surrounding the lawsuit and rebranding. It also reported a 114% increase in sales over that period.The Charleston store opening on April 25 provided a major payoff. Club Coastal recorded $30,000 in sales that day, its highest single-day figure at the time, according to Sent News. A charm necklace was sold approximately every 70 seconds during the opening.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
